clean.png: Attention is the mind's selective hold on one object at the expense of others. William James described it as withdrawal from some things in order to deal effectively with others. The metaphor is useful because it treats focus as a budget rather than a switch. Every additional demand on that budget makes the remaining work shallower and slower. A quiet room is not a luxury; it is a reduction in the number of competing bids for the same resources. Designing the environment is therefore a more reliable strategy than relying on willpower alone. Habit begins as a deliberate choice and ends as a background process. A cue opens the sequence, a routine carries it, and a reward closes the loop. Because the cue is usually environmental, changing the room changes the behaviour more reliably than changing the intention. People who appear disciplined often have simply arranged their surroundings so that the desired action is the easiest one available. The practical question is not how to want something more, but how to make it require less friction. Memory is reconstructive rather than photographic. Each retrieval reopens a trace and writes it down again with the context of the present moment. That is why confident recollection can still be mistaken, and why re-reading feels fluent without producing durable knowledge. Retrieval practice is harder and feels less productive, yet it strengthens the trace precisely because it requires effort. Spacing those attempts across days gives the system time to forget a little, which is the condition under which the next attempt is useful.

dense_columns.png: A library is an argument about what deserves to be remembered. Selection is never neutral: every shelf excludes more than it includes. The useful question is not whether a canon exists, but who assembled it, for what purpose, and what it leaves out. Reading widely is not the same as reading indiscriminately. A good list gives you a sequence, a reason for the sequence, and permission to stop. Habit begins as a deliberate choice and ends as a background process. A note without a source is a rumour; a note without a question is a transcription. The strongest notes record the claim, the evidence, and the disagreement it provoked. Linking two notes is often more useful than adding a third. Over time the graph of links becomes the real document, and the original text becomes its evidence base.
